Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Australia's reply. Well, a surprise at the top of the order as Glenn Maxwell walks out to open the innings alongside Mitchell Marsh. Akeal Hosein will kickstart proceedings. Let's play....
... THE RUN CHASE ...

For Aussies, Adam Zampa was comfortably the pick of the bowlers, finishing with figures of 4-0-29-3. He used the slowness of the surface well. Apart from Zampa, Nathan Ellis and Glenn Maxwell picked up two each as they too used the deck well. Australia will back themselves to chase this down while West Indies will be on the hunt for early wickets to put the tourists on the back foot. Back in a bit for the second innings.

Andre Russell is in for a chat. He says he just didn’t want to finish on a losing note, admitting that while the team had played good cricket in patches, they were about 20 runs short, given how the wicket was playing. He stresses the importance of signing off with a win and confesses to feeling nervous performing in front of his home crowd for the final time. Mentions that he loves playing the big hits.

After the openers perished, there was a bit of a lull period as the middle order batters got starts but couldn’t quite kick on. However, a late flourish from Andre Russell, in his last game, and then some good hits down the order from Gudakesh Motie ensured Windies crossed the 170-run mark.

So West Indies finish with 172 on the board. With the wicket on the slower side, one would think it's round about par. The innings started with a good opening stand, as the duo of Shai Hope and Brandon King put on 63 for the first wicket. The latter in particular was the dominator as he went on to score 51 before losing his wicket to Adam Zampa.

A bye to end the innings! Slower one, going across the batter, just inside the tramline, Gudakesh Motie has a swing at it but fails to lay any bat on it. The batters set off for a bye and Josh Inglis misses the underarm throw at the batting end. 12 runs off the final over. West Indies end up with 172 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Andre Russell is given a guard of honour by the two teams as he walks onto the field. Jamaica's Minister of Sport and Culture, Olivia Grange, greets him and presents him with a memento. Time to get the second T20I underway. Mitchell Marsh leads his troops out onto the park. They are followed by the two openers of West Indies, Shai Hope and Brandon King. The tourists are starting with spin in the form of the debutant, Matthew Kuhnemann. Kuhnemann to King with a slip in place. Here we go!

Time to hear from Cooper Connolly. He starts by saying that it’s nice to represent the country and he always tries to be involved in the game as much as possible. On playing against Windies, he says that it's super exciting and with a good amount of firepower in both teams, it's always a good challenge. On representing Australia, he says it’s just about enjoying the experience and enjoying every moment of it. On asked about bowling in the Powerplay, he feels it’s a tough challenge to bowl with two fielders out but he tries to change his pace and be less predictable and it worked for him in the last game. On asked about his own game, he mentions that he is trying to learn as much as he can and trying to talk with coaches to get as much information as possible. On asked about what Australia need to do to win today, he feels they should stick to the process and back themselves.

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is near the deck. He informs us that we are back on pitch number 3, and it has resulted in equidistant square boundaries measuring 64 metres. Jimmy Adams joins him and he says that these are perfect batting conditions with the surface being hard and firm. Mentions that the bounce was true in the first game and that is exactly what the batters want. Feels that bowlers will need to be smart and use their variations. Adds that Australia took pace off very well in the last game and West Indies will have to take a leaf out of their book.

Shimron Hetmyer is in for a chat. On the loss in the 1st game, he says they would look to put that side and take the learnings and he feels it’s a one-off loss. On his finishing role, he says it’s more about the mindset of keeping the mind open because, as a finisher, he feels batters don’t know how many balls they will get to bat. On the preparation for the T20 World Cup, he says it's better to keep playing together and keep practising. On Russell’s last game in T20s, he says that the one word he would like to define Russell is ‘muscle’.

Visuals from the Aussie huddle are in where left-arm spinner, Matthew Kuhnemann, receives his maiden T20I cap from Adam Zampa. Kuhnemann becomes the 113th man to represent Australia in T20Is. Not far from them, in the West Indies huddle, Andre Russell is being greeted with hugs and smiles from his teammates ahead of his last international dance.

Australia (Playing XI) - Mitchell Marsh (C), Josh Inglis, Cameron Green, Glenn Maxwell, Tim David (In for Jake Fraser-McGurk), Mitchell Owen, Cooper Connolly, Ben Dwarshuis, Nathan Ellis, Matthew Kuhnemann (On T20I debut) (In for Sean Abbott), Adam Zampa.

West Indies (Unchanged Playing XI) - Brandon King, Shai Hope (C/WK), Roston Chase, Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell, Andre Russell, Sherfane Rutherford, Jason Holder, Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein.

The captain of West Indies, Shai Hope says that they have been doing well with the bat in recent years and it is about finishing better. Mentions that with the ball, it is very important to execute the plans and be clinical. Informs that they are going with the same team as the last game.

The captain of Australia, Mitchell Marsh says that they will bowl first and he does not expect the wicket to change much. He adds that 200 seems to be par on this wicket and says that his bowlers did well in the last game to restrict WI and hopefully they will do the job again. He mentions that in the last game, the debutant Mitchell Owen did well and he expects that all the batters should bat with that kind of freedom to succeed in T20s. Informs that they have made two changes with Tim David coming in for Jake Fraser-McGurk and Matthew Kuhnemann making his T20I debut, replacing Sean Abbott.
TOSS - Australia have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

On the other hand, for the West Indies, in the 1st game, the top order did more than a decent job, as the hosts were 159/2 at one point. But a mega collapse saw them lose their way as the last 27 balls of their innings produced only 30 runs as the Windies lost 6 wickets. Given that these are early days in the series, the Windies might just want to back their 11 from the 1st game. Will the visitors stay unbeaten on the tour and take a 2-0 lead in the T20I series, or will the men from the Caribbean score the equaliser, making it 1-1? We shall find out.

In the first game, Australia registered a fairly comfortable win as fifties from Mitchell Owen and Cameron Green helped them chase down the target of 190 in the penultimate over. In the bowling department, Ben Dwarshuis was the hero, as he got a four-fer to his name. Overall, everyone chipped in with the bat or ball in hand, and it will be hard to see Aussies changing the winning combination going into this game.

Hello and welcome to the 2nd game of this five-match T20I series between the West Indies and Australia at Sabina Park in Kingston. The visitors are yet to lose a game on this tour, and they would look to continue their winning streak. The West Indies, on the other hand, would be desperate to get a win in their most preferred format. Much of the spotlight in front of his home crowd will be on Andre Russell as he bids adieu to international cricket after this game.
... MATCH DAY ...

Celebrate Kingston’s own as the West Indies gear up for a high-emotion 2nd T20I against Australia - this one’s not just a match, it’s Andre Russell’s final international appearance. Playing in his hometown, Russell will bring the curtain down on a memorable career that includes two T20 World Cup titles. He’ll be fired up to deliver one final show in front of a roaring Jamaican crowd. Australia come into this clash riding high after a thrilling 3-wicket win in the series opener. Mitchell Owen stole the spotlight with a blistering half-century on debut, while Cameron Green’s composed knock ensured they crossed the line. They’ll also be buoyed by the form of Josh Inglis at the top and the pace trio of Nathan Ellis, Ben Dwarshuis, and Sean Abbott, who offer depth and variety with the ball. Adam Zampa also has a great record in the Caribbean and will look to slow things down in the middle overs with his accurate spin bowling. However, their top order showed signs of wobble and could come under pressure if early wickets fall. But having the likes of skipper Mitchell Marsh and Glenn Maxwell only adds even more destruction on the batting front. West Indies had dominated much of their innings in the first T20I with fifties from Roston Chase and Shai Hope, both anchoring the innings well, but the lack of finishing firepower in the lower order hurt them. With Nicholas Pooran retired and Russell set for a farewell game, a lot will rest on experienced names like Shimron Hetmyer who looked in great touch, Romario Shepherd, and Rovman Powell to step up. Their strength lies in their all-round options and power hitters, but the death bowling remains a concern, especially after the way they let the game slip late. They will rely on the likes of Alzarri Joseph and Jason Holder to deliver. With emotions running high and their backs against the wall, West Indies will need to deliver a more complete performance, while Australia will look to ride their new heroes and go 2-0 up. Expect a fiery contest with a packed Sabina Park backing their hometown hero one last time.
